senses.definition: To sit or balance on a high or narrow spot.
senses.example: The robin perched on a fence post.

senses.definition: A high or narrow place where a bird or another animal can rest.
senses.example: The parakeet hopped onto its perch.

senses.definition: One of several kinds of fish with pointed spines in their fins.
senses.example: A small perch swam near the reeds.

senses.definition: A liquid or substance used for its pleasant smell.
senses.example: The perfume smelled faintly like lemons.

senses.definition: To fill a place or thing with a pleasant smell.
senses.example: The blooming flowers perfumed the room.

senses.definition: A tube with mirrors or similar parts that lets someone see over or around something blocking the view.
senses.example: We used a cardboard periscope to see over the wall.

senses.definition: An extra advantage or benefit.
senses.example: One perk of joining the club was getting to try the new games first.

senses.definition: To make or become more lively or alert, often used with “up.”
senses.example: The dog's ears perked up when we opened the back door.

senses.definition: To keep trying even when a task is difficult or takes a long time.
senses.example: She persevered until she could play the song without stopping.

senses.definition: To get someone to believe or do something by giving them reasons.
senses.example: I persuaded my friends to try a shorter route by showing them the map.

senses.definition: A picture made with a camera.
senses.example: I took a photograph of the round moon over the barn.

senses.definition: To use a camera to take a picture of something.
senses.example: We photographed a new leaf on the plant every day.

senses.definition: A food, often a cucumber, preserved in salty or sour liquid.
senses.example: I put a crunchy pickle next to my sandwich.

senses.definition: A difficult or awkward situation, usually in the phrase “in a pickle.”
senses.example: We were in a pickle when we lost the key to the shed.

senses.definition: To preserve food by keeping it in a liquid such as vinegar or salt water.
senses.example: The shop sold carrots pickled with garlic.

senses.definition: A raised structure that extends from land over water.
senses.example: We walked to the end of the pier to watch the boats.

senses.definition: A plump bird with a short neck often seen walking or flying in towns and cities.
senses.example: A pigeon looked for crumbs below the bench.

senses.definition: A length of hair tied together at one side or at the back of the head, sometimes braided.
senses.example: I tied one pigtail with a green ribbon.

senses.definition: A tall, strong post or upright structure that can hold up part of a building.
senses.example: A stone pillar stood at each corner of the porch.

senses.definition: A soft pad used to rest your head on.
senses.example: I slipped the clean cover over my pillow.

senses.definition: A person who flies an aircraft or guides a vessel through difficult water.
senses.example: Our pilot spoke to the passengers before the plane landed.

senses.definition: To fly or steer a vehicle or to guide something through a first test.
senses.example: She piloted the small aircraft over the coast.

senses.definition: A structure with overlapping scales that holds or produces seeds on a pine tree, usually used to mean the larger seed cone.
senses.example: A pinecone fell off the tree and bounced onto the path.

senses.definition: A unit for measuring liquids, or in some cases dry goods.
senses.example: We picked a pint of blueberries at the farm.

senses.definition: A toy with brightly colored blades that turn in the wind on the end of a handle.
senses.example: I held the pinwheel up so the breeze could make it spin.

senses.definition: A person who is among the first in a place or field to try a new way of doing something.
senses.example: The exhibit honored a pioneer of radio broadcasting.

senses.definition: To be among the first to create or use a new idea or method.
senses.example: She pioneered a simple way to build lighter kites.

senses.definition: An outdoor place set aside for children to play, often with equipment such as swings and slides.
senses.example: The playground had a climbing wall shaped like a boat.

senses.definition: To walk slowly with heavy steps or keep working in a slow, steady way.
senses.example: We plodded through wet sand on our way back to the tent.

senses.definition: To drop with a soft, hollow sound or to sit down heavily.
senses.example: A piece of mud plopped into the water.

senses.definition: A soft hollow sound made by something dropping.
senses.example: I heard a plop when the frog jumped.

senses.definition: A person who installs or repairs pipes and equipment that carry water or waste.
senses.example: The plumber fixed a leaking pipe under the sink.

senses.definition: To fall straight down or decrease very quickly.
senses.example: The temperature plummeted after sunset.

senses.definition: In grammar, used to show that you are talking about more than one.
senses.example: “Boxes” is the plural form of “box.”

senses.definition: The form of a word used to mean more than one person or thing.
senses.example: The plural of “child” is “children.”

senses.definition: A covered space outside the entrance of a building.
senses.example: We left our muddy boots on the porch.

senses.definition: A thick soft food made by cooking grain such as oats in water or milk.
senses.example: I added raisins to my bowl of porridge.

senses.definition: A stiff card used for sending a short message in the mail without an envelope.
senses.example: I mailed my friend a postcard with a picture of the beach.

senses.definition: To move a planned event or action to a later time.
senses.example: We postponed our picnic until the rain stopped.

senses.definition: A small bag or pocket that carries or protects something.
senses.example: I slipped the marbles into a cloth pouch.

senses.definition: To jump suddenly toward something to grab it or land on it.
senses.example: The kitten pounced on the ball of yarn.

senses.definition: A trick meant to surprise or amuse someone.
senses.example: I played a silly prank by putting a toy duck in the pencil cup.

senses.definition: To play a trick on someone as a joke.
senses.example: My family pranked me with a paper spider in the cookie jar.

senses.definition: To come before something in time or order.
senses.example: A short warm-up preceded the soccer game.

senses.definition: A small sharp point on the surface of a plant, animal, or other object.
senses.example: One prickle on the stem caught my sleeve.

senses.definition: To feel as if many tiny points are touching the skin, or to make that feeling happen.
senses.example: My skin prickled when I walked out into the cold.

senses.definition: A basic rule or belief that guides how you act or helps explain how something works.
senses.example: One principle of our team was to make sure everyone got a turn.

senses.definition: A solid shape with matching parallel ends joined by flat sides.
senses.example: The triangular prism on my desk had matching triangles at its ends.

senses.definition: A clear object with flat sides that can bend light, sometimes spreading white light into colors.
senses.example: A prism hanging in the window cast colors on the wall.

senses.definition: To say a word or sound in a particular way.
senses.example: Could you show me how to pronounce the name on this map?

senses.definition: An object used by an actor in a show.
senses.example: The wooden key was a prop in the school play.

senses.definition: To hold something up or keep it in position by putting another thing against it.
senses.example: We propped the door open with a shoe.

senses.definition: To push or drive something forward.
senses.example: The turning wheels propelled the cart down the path.

senses.definition: A set of blades that spin to move air or water and push a vehicle.
senses.example: The boat's propeller sent a stream of bubbles behind it.

senses.definition: Writing in ordinary sentences and paragraphs rather than in lines of poetry.
senses.example: The book tells one chapter in verse and the next in prose.

senses.definition: To stick out from or beyond a surface.
senses.example: A corner of the blanket protruded from the closed box.

senses.definition: A short well-known saying that gives advice or shares a general idea about life.
senses.example: “Many hands make light work” is a proverb about helping each other.

senses.definition: To move quietly while watching or looking for something.
senses.example: The cat prowled around the garden after dark.

senses.definition: A seabird with a thick, brightly colored bill during the breeding season.
senses.example: A puffin carried small fish back to its nest.

senses.definition: A large wild cat found in the Americas, also called a cougar or mountain lion.
senses.example: A wildlife camera caught a puma walking quietly at night.

senses.definition: A round or ridged squash, often orange, with firm flesh and many seeds.
senses.example: We planted a pumpkin seed at one edge of the garden.

senses.definition: Marks in writing, such as periods and question marks, that help show how the words fit together or should be read.
senses.example: We checked the punctuation before turning in our stories.

senses.definition: Done with a clear aim or with determination.
senses.example: She took purposeful steps toward the stage even though she was nervous.

senses.definition: A small bag used to carry money or personal things.
senses.example: I found the bus pass inside my purse.

senses.definition: To draw the lips together into a small rounded shape.
senses.example: He pursed his lips as he tried to whistle.

senses.definition: A problem, picture, or game meant to be worked out by thinking.
senses.example: We finished the puzzle and saw a picture of a sailboat.

senses.definition: To make someone think hard because something is confusing or unexpected.
senses.example: The footprints in the dry sand puzzled me.
